chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, al-Hasan, from his father, Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Uthman ibn Isa narrated from al-Mu'alla ibn Abi Shihab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'O my father! What is the reward for one who visits you?' He (the Messenger of Allah) replied: 'O my son! Whoever visits me while I am alive or after I am dead, or visits your father, or visits your brother, or visits you, it becomes a duty upon me to visit them on the Day of Judgment and to deliver them from their sins.'

key_terms.أَبَاكَ: Your father (referring to Imam Ali in this context)
key_terms.أَخَاكَ: Your brother (referring to Imam Hasan in this context)
key_terms.أُخَلِّصَهُ: To deliver/save him, specifically from sins in this context
key_terms.حَقّاً عَلَيَّ: It becomes a duty upon me, indicating a guaranteed divine promise
key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (Ziyarah), a devotional act of visiting shrines or graves of holy figures

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet and the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) asks the Prophet (s.a.w.) about the reward for visiting him, receiving a promise of divine reciprocation where the Prophet visits the visitor on the Day of Judgment to absolve them of sins. This highlights the Shia concept of *Ziyarah* not merely as a physical act but as a spiritual bond that secures intercession and purification, emphasizing the enduring presence of the Ahl al-Bayt in the afterlife.
